newsitem.title: USA: Calif. measure would create new transit authority.
newsitem.headline: Calif. measure would create new transit authority.

text.p: A California state legislator has introduced a bill that would create an authority that could construct a new transportation center in Riverside County using tax-exempt bonds.

State Senator Dave Kelley's measure would create the East Valley Intermodal Transportation Authority (EVITA). The authority would construct, operate and maintain the East Valley Intermodal Transportation Center in Indio, California.
The center, which would operate independently of the city of Indio and its general fund, would receive funding through a combination of state and matching local funds.

The authority would be authorized to issue general and special revenue bonds for acquisition and construction. The total amount of bonds outstanding would not exceed $100 million at any one time, according to legislation.z The bonds would constitute obligations of the authority alone, and neither the payment of the principal or interest of any bond would constitute a debt, liability or obligation of the state of California, the legislation said.
The measure -- Senate Bill 459 -- has yet to be assigned to a legislative committee for review.
